title: Cross-functional new hire playbook - 90d guild onboarding (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, pragmatic playbook for hiring and onboarding cross-functional hires (engineer + product-adjacent roles) using a small ‘guild’ model: cohort-style first 90 days + mentor rotation. Target: reduce time-to-impact, normalize interview signals, and create a predictable, scalable first-90-day experience for mid-senior ICs.

Scope:
- Applies to HW/SRE-adjacent engineers, platform PM-like product managers, developer experience engineers, and solutions-engineering hires that will cross Eng <> Product org boundaries.
- Not for exec hires or pure sales/CS roles (separate playbook).

One-line hiring thesis:
Hire for complementary craft + stakeholder fluency. Use a narrow, repeatable interview rubric and a 90-day guild-first onboarding to accelerate network effects inside the org.

High-level timeline (target SLAs):
- Requisition -> first screen: 6 business days
- Onsite / loop scheduled after phone screen: within 10 business days
- Offer out after onsite: 3 business days
- Start date -> 1st-week buddy assigned: Day 0 (pre-start)
- 30/60/90 checkpoints: weeks 4, 8, 12
(Notes: track times in JIRA-Acquisition board; if >2 weeks at any stage escalate to recruiting lead)

Interview rubric (single-page, simplified for panel):
Score: 1–5 (1 = not demonstrated, 5 = strong evidence)
Core dimensions (weight in parens):
- Technical craft / problem solving (40%) – coding/system design/operational judgement appropriate to role
- Collaboration & stakeholder navigation (25%) – signals: cross-team examples, conflict resolution, partnership outcomes
- Product thinking & tradeoffs (15%) – hypothesis-driven decisions, metrics awareness, tradeoff articulation
- Ownership & deliverability (10%) – shipped examples, timelines, risk mitigation
- Diversity & inclusivity behaviors (10%) – mentoring, inclusive decision making, hiring bias awareness

Calibration notes for interviewers:
- Use STARs. Ask for artifacts (PR links, charts) when possible. If candidate is remote and cannot share, accept precise walkthroughs.
- For cross-functional hires prioritize examples where they negotiated tradeoffs under ambiguity (e.g., shipping a feature with infra constraints).
- Avoid expensive whiteboard-only puzzles. For systems questions, prefer small scoped design problems with real constraints (latency, cost, reliability).

Sample question bank (role-tailored):
- Eng/platform: "Describe a time you reduced tail latency for a production endpoint. What tradeoffs did you make? How did you validate improvement?"
- DevX/SDK: "Walk me through a breaking SDK change you shipped. How did you communicate migration steps to customers/internal teams?"
- Solutions/SE: "Give an example where you had to say 'no' to a customer request. How did you keep the relationship intact?"
- Product-adjacent: "How do you evaluate whether a small UX change is worth a platform-level investment? Which metrics would you track?"

Panel composition guidance:
- 4-interviewer loop (ideal): 1x craft (senior engineer), 1x system owner (peer), 1x PM/partner, 1x manager or bar-raiser (hiring manager optional).
- Include at least one interviewer with documented calibration (has done >5 hires in last 12 months).
- For senior hires, add a 30-min executive alignment conversation before offer.

Scoring & decision flow:
- Each interviewer submits rubric within 24h. Recruiting synthesizes a one-paragraph summary and recommends (hire/no-hire/hold) to hiring committee.
- Hiring committee decision within 48h of final loop. Committee comprises hiring manager, recruiter, 1 engineering leader, and 1 people-ops rep.
- Tie-breaker: if split, request 1 additional focused interview (2–3 questions) rather than call multiple new interviewers.

Offer strategy and comp notes:
- Role band reference: use rubric -> target midpoint + market uplift (Engineering comp sheet v3).
- Use early-call compensation template if candidate has competing offer; coordinate with recruiting lead and finance.
- For cross-functional hires emphasize equity cliff timing + mentorship allocation (explicit mentor hours per month).

Guild onboarding model (what makes this playbook unique):
- New hires with similar onboarding signals are grouped into a small guild (2–6 people) for first 4 weeks to run weekly "shadow sprints" and guild demos. Guild includes 1 mentor rotation per week (see Mentor rotation below).
- Guild topics: system tour, core infra primitives (how Redwood serves models), common debugging playbooks, deploying a small infra change, and cross-team intro workshops.
- Outcomes: each guild run concludes with a micro-project (merged PR + short demo) to surface early-owned output.

Mentor rotation (concrete):
- Week 0 (pre-start): assigned primary buddy (buddy checklist).
- Weeks 1–4: rotate guild mentors weekly; each mentor leads a focused 90-min workshop + 30-min office hours. Mentors are senior ICs from Eng/Platform/DevX/Product.
- Weeks 5–12: primary mentor remains; secondary mentors by request.
- Mentorship expectations (for mentors): 2–4 hours/week active time, proactive onboarding tasks, feedback to people-ops for calibration.

First-week checklist (to be completed by manager + buddy):
- Pre-start: account creation, laptop shipment confirmed, first-week calendar (meetings + onboarding sessions) sent.
- Day 0: welcome + org map, buddy intro, Slack channel add, Min 1:1 scheduled with manager for day 2.
- Day 1–5: infra walkthru, local dev setup, run a tiny smoke test end-to-end (template task in GH), join guild intro.
- Admin: payroll paperwork, benefits orientation, security training (complete by day 7).

30/60/90 sample goals (engineer example):
- 30d: dev env healthy, merged a small infra or bugfix PR, completed 3 cross-team intros, publish a short 'what I learned' note to guild channel.
- 60d: own a small feature or infra task end-to-end, reduce or document a flaky test or alert, lead a guild demo.
- 90d: measurable impact (latency improvement, cost saving, or feature shipped), feedback session with manager and people-ops, plan next 6 months.

Onboarding deliverables (artifact expectations):
- 1-pager: "Area takeover" — what the hire thinks they can own in 3–6 months (due week 4).
- 1 tech writeup: walkthrough of a system area they touched (due week 8).
- Guild demo recording + short retrospective (week 4).

Calibration & interviewer training notes:
- People-ops runs quarterly calibration sessions with a focus on cross-functional signal normalization (share top-voted interview transcripts as examples).
- Reminder: avoid biasing safe hires only — look for growth trajectory signals.

Diversity & hiring slates:
- Must request diverse slate from recruiting for all non-senior IC roles; for senior ICs use reasonable efforts and document search constraints.
- For panels, include at least one interviewer from different functional background when possible (e.g., a DevEx interviewer on an infra panel).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide measurable success metric for the guild model (time-to-first-merge vs time-to-independent-work?) — propose A/B: cohort vs individual onboarding for next 6 months.
- Mentor stipend / recognition: need budget ask to people-ops/finance for mentor hours recognition.
- Create a small "onboarding micro-project" template in GH (TODO: @Jamie create PR).

Quick links / references (working):
- Onboarding templates repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding
- People-ops hiring metrics board: https://jira.redwood.ai/board/RECRUIT-OPS
- Confluence: Onboarding central (ONBRD-341)

Notes to self: keep this doc short, link to longer artifacts not repeat. Run first pilot guild (4 hires) in Q1 2026; collect feedback via NPS + manager qualitative notes.

Action items (owners):
- Priya: finalize micro-project template + brief the guild mentors (Due: 2025-12-08).
- Ethan: add interview question bank to interviewers’ playbook and schedule calibration (Due: 2025-12-15).
- Marina: draft mentor recognition proposal for finance (Due: 2026-01-10).

Rough version history:
- 2025-10-12 created (initial idea notes)
- 2025-11-07 added detailed rubric and mentor rotation model
- 2025-12-01 updated SLAs and action owners

End of doc — comments welcome (this is intentionally opinionated + pragmatic; expect iteration).
